name: SSC Phrasal Verbs
description: Important phrasal verbs for SSC English with meanings and memorable examples.

cards.definition:
Meaning: to explain the reason for something

Example: The missing receipt accounted for the panic in the accounts room.

Meaning: to take action based on advice or information

Example: The officer acted on the tip before the rumour grew legs.

Meaning: to perform or express through actions

Example: The child acted out the story with more drama than the original.

Meaning: to make sense or total correctly

Example: His excuse did not add up, especially after the CCTV footage arrived.

Meaning: to result in a total or final meaning

Example: Small daily mistakes can add up to a big loss in marks.

Meaning: to ask about someone's health or welfare

Example: Grandmother asked after everyone, including the neighbour's parrot.

Meaning: to request something

Example: He asked for extra time after wasting the first ten minutes sharpening a pencil.

Meaning: to withdraw from a position or argument

Example: The bully backed down when the quiet boy showed unusual confidence.

Meaning: to withdraw from a promise or plan

Example: He backed out of the trip after hearing the word trekking.

Meaning: to support or make a copy

Example: Always back up your notes before the laptop decides to become philosophical.

Meaning: to support or confirm

Example: The witness's statement bore out the police theory.

Meaning: to be patient with

Example: Bear with me while I explain why this simple rule has five exceptions.

Meaning: to explode or become very angry

Example: The pressure cooker blew up like it had resigned from kitchen service.

Meaning: to separate from a group

Example: The cyclist broke away from the group near the final turn.

Meaning: to stop working or lose emotional control

Example: The old scooter broke down exactly in front of the mechanic's shop.

Meaning: to enter by force or interrupt

Example: Thieves broke in at night, but the dog became the security department.

Meaning: to enter by force or suddenly start doing something

Example: She broke into laughter during the very serious speech.

Meaning: to end suddenly

Example: The talks broke off when both sides discovered they were equally stubborn.

Meaning: to start suddenly

Example: A fire broke out in the warehouse after a careless spark.

Meaning: to make an important discovery or progress

Example: Scientists broke through after years of patient research.

Meaning: to end a relationship or disperse

Example: The meeting broke up when the power went out.

Meaning: to cause something to happen

Example: One honest decision can bring about real change.

Meaning: to return something or revive a memory

Example: The old song brought back memories of school assemblies.

Meaning: to reduce or defeat

Example: Strict action brought down the number of fake applications.

Meaning: to move to an earlier time or present for discussion

Example: The meeting was brought forward because the boss had travel plans.

Meaning: to introduce or earn

Example: The new policy brought in stricter rules.

Meaning: to publish or reveal

Example: The crisis brought out the best in the volunteers.

Meaning: to raise a child or mention a topic

Example: She brought up the issue just when everyone thought lunch was safe.

Meaning: to ignore or dismiss

Example: He brushed aside the warning and then met the exact problem.

Meaning: to revise or improve a skill

Example: Brush up your grammar before the exam starts asking personal questions.

Meaning: to develop gradually

Example: Daily revision builds up confidence quietly.

Meaning: to meet unexpectedly

Example: I bumped into my school friend at the railway station.

Meaning: to become exhausted from overwork

Example: He burned out after studying sixteen hours a day with zero strategy.

Meaning: to return a phone call

Example: She called back after the phone stopped behaving like a brick.

Meaning: to demand or require

Example: The situation calls for patience, not WhatsApp expertise.

Meaning: to cancel

Example: The picnic was called off because the sky joined the opposition.

Meaning: to visit or request formally

Example: The teacher called on the student to explain the answer.

Meaning: to phone or summon

Example: He called up his friend for notes two hours before the test.

Meaning: to become too excited or emotional

Example: The speaker got carried away and turned a five-minute talk into a documentary.

Meaning: to continue

Example: Carry on with your work even if motivation is absent.

Meaning: to perform or complete

Example: The team carried out the survey in three villages.

Meaning: to become popular or understand

Example: The new slang caught on faster than the teacher expected.

Meaning: to reach the same level

Example: She studied every morning to catch up with the class.

Meaning: to register arrival

Example: We checked in at the hotel after the train tested our patience.

Meaning: to examine or leave a hotel

Example: Check out this rule before choosing the answer.

Meaning: to remove things

Example: Clear away the cups before the table becomes an archaeological site.

Meaning: to explain or become better

Example: The teacher cleared up the confusion with one good example.

Meaning: to find or meet by chance

Example: I came across an old admit card inside a forgotten notebook.

Meaning: to progress or accompany

Example: The project is coming along better than our first nervous plan.

Meaning: to break into pieces

Example: The cheap bag came apart during the bus ride.

Meaning: to obtain or visit briefly

Example: Good second-hand books are hard to come by.

Meaning: to become ill with

Example: He came down with fever just before the match.

Meaning: to volunteer or present oneself

Example: A witness came forward after seeing the news.

Meaning: to succeed or become detached

Example: The sticker came off, but the glue stayed like a permanent resident.

Meaning: to be published or become known

Example: The result came out at midnight and destroyed everyone's sleep.

Meaning: to visit

Example: Come over after class and we will compare notes.

Meaning: to survive or succeed despite difficulty

Example: The village came through the flood with remarkable courage.

Meaning: to arise or be mentioned

Example: This phrasal verb came up in last year's paper.

Meaning: to produce an idea or solution

Example: She came up with a shortcut that actually worked.

Meaning: to rely on

Example: You can count on a good friend, not on last-minute luck.

Meaning: to reduce

Example: Cut down screen time before it cuts down your marks.

Meaning: to disconnect or isolate

Example: The village was cut off after the bridge collapsed.

Meaning: to remove or stop

Example: Cut out unnecessary words from the essay.

Meaning: to trade in something

Example: The shop deals in old coins and rare stamps.

Meaning: to handle or manage

Example: A calm mind deals with tough questions better.

Meaning: to become weaker

Example: The noise died down after the principal entered.

Meaning: to abolish or remove

Example: The school did away with the old uniform rule.

Meaning: to fasten or renovate

Example: Do up your shoelaces before running like a hero.

Meaning: to manage without

Example: We had to do without electricity for three hours.

Meaning: to prepare a written plan or document

Example: The lawyer drew up the agreement carefully.

Meaning: to visit casually

Example: He dropped in without warning and found everyone cleaning.

Meaning: to fall asleep or leave someone somewhere

Example: The baby dropped off while the lullaby was still warming up.

Meaning: to leave a course or competition

Example: He dropped out of the race after an injury.

Meaning: to eat at a restaurant

Example: They ate out after burning the experimental dinner.

Meaning: to finally reach a state or situation

Example: He ignored directions and ended up near the bus depot.

Meaning: to accept and deal with a problem

Example: Face up to your mistakes before they become habits.

Meaning: to break into pieces or collapse emotionally

Example: The plan fell apart when nobody brought the charger.

Meaning: to fail to keep up

Example: He fell behind because he revised only during panic season.

Meaning: to be deceived by or fall in love with

Example: Do not fall for offers that look richer than common sense.

Meaning: to quarrel

Example: The two friends fell out over a borrowed bicycle.

Meaning: to fail to happen

Example: The deal fell through at the last moment.

Meaning: to understand or solve

Example: She figured out the answer after drawing a tiny diagram.

Meaning: to complete a form or substitute temporarily

Example: Fill in the blanks carefully, especially the ones that look too easy.

Meaning: to discover

Example: The teacher found out who had copied the homework.

Meaning: to belong or adjust

Example: The new student fit in quickly because he shared snacks.

Meaning: to arrange or repair

Example: They fixed up a meeting before the deadline became dangerous.

Meaning: to communicate successfully

Example: A good example gets across the rule faster than a lecture.

Meaning: to have a friendly relationship

Example: The two neighbours get along because both dislike loud music.

Meaning: to move from place to place or avoid a rule

Example: He tried to get around the rule but met the invigilator.

Meaning: to suggest or imply

Example: What are you getting at with that mysterious smile?

Meaning: to escape

Example: The thief got away because everyone was arguing about directions.

Meaning: to avoid punishment

Example: He thought he would get away with cheating, but the CCTV had better memory.

Meaning: to return

Example: Get back before dinner or face family-level questioning.

Meaning: to manage with difficulty

Example: He got by on little money and a lot of jugaad.

Meaning: to descend or make someone sad

Example: Do not let one wrong answer get you down.

Meaning: to start doing something seriously

Example: Get down to revision before the syllabus starts laughing.

Meaning: to enter or arrive

Example: The train got in late, which surprised nobody.

Meaning: to enter or become involved

Example: He got into trouble after forwarding a fake message.

Meaning: to leave a bus/train or escape punishment

Example: We got off the bus near the post office.

Meaning: to board or progress

Example: Get on the train before the whistle becomes personal.

Meaning: to leave or become known

Example: The secret got out before the party began.

Meaning: to recover from

Example: She got over the disappointment and tried again.

Meaning: to pass or complete successfully

Example: He got through the exam by staying calm.

Meaning: to meet or gather

Example: The group got together to plan the project.

Meaning: to rise from bed or sitting position

Example: Get up early before the alarm loses self-respect.

Meaning: to reveal or donate

Example: His nervous smile gave away the secret.

Meaning: to return

Example: Give back the pen before it joins your permanent collection.

Meaning: to surrender

Example: After three hours of bargaining, the shopkeeper gave in.

Meaning: to emit

Example: The flowers gave off a sweet smell.

Meaning: to distribute or stop functioning

Example: The teacher gave out the papers and silence entered the room.

Meaning: to quit or stop trying

Example: Do not give up because one mock test behaved badly.

Meaning: to pursue

Example: The police went after the gang at dawn.

Meaning: to proceed

Example: Go ahead with the plan if the documents are ready.

Meaning: to agree or cooperate

Example: She went along with the idea after seeing the evidence.

Meaning: to fail to keep a promise

Example: He went back on his promise and lost trust.

Meaning: to decrease

Example: The temperature went down after the rain.

Meaning: to choose or try to get

Example: She went for the safer option in the exam.

Meaning: to explode, ring, or stop being fresh

Example: The alarm went off at five, and everyone ignored it professionally.

Meaning: to continue

Example: The speaker went on until even the microphone looked tired.

Meaning: to stop burning or leave socially

Example: The lights went out during the final over.

Meaning: to review

Example: Go over your answers before submitting.

Meaning: to experience or examine carefully

Example: She went through the file line by line.

Meaning: to increase

Example: Prices went up faster than pocket money.

Meaning: to become an adult

Example: Grow up does not only mean age, it also means maturity.

Meaning: to submit

Example: Hand in your answer sheet before the bell rings.

Meaning: to distribute

Example: The monitor handed out notebooks like election pamphlets.

Meaning: to wait or spend time idly

Example: Do not hang around the exam centre after the paper.

Meaning: to end a phone call

Example: She hung up when the sales call became too friendly.

Meaning: to move toward

Example: Dark clouds headed for the city like a warning.

Meaning: to restrain or hide

Example: He held back tears after missing the final selection.

Meaning: to wait or grip tightly

Example: Hold on, the answer is simpler than it looks.

Meaning: to delay or support

Example: Traffic was held up by a wedding procession.

Meaning: to avoid or stay at a distance

Example: Keep away from rumours before exams.

Meaning: to withhold

Example: The teacher kept back a few students for extra practice.

Meaning: to stay away from

Example: Keep off the wet floor unless you want free skating.

Meaning: to continue

Example: Keep on revising until the rule feels natural.

Meaning: to maintain pace or level

Example: She kept up with the class by revising daily.

Meaning: to stay at the same level as

Example: It is hard to keep up with fast-changing technology.

Meaning: to hit and make fall

Example: The storm knocked down an old signboard.

Meaning: to make unconscious or defeat

Example: The boxer was knocked out in the final round.

Meaning: to dismiss from work

Example: The company laid off workers during the crisis.

Meaning: to forget or abandon

Example: He left behind his admit card and carried only confidence.

Meaning: to omit

Example: Do not leave out important steps in a grammar answer.

Meaning: to disappoint

Example: He let down his team by arriving late.

Meaning: to excuse or release lightly

Example: The teacher let him off with a warning.

Meaning: to take care of

Example: Look after your books before they vanish into the house.

Meaning: to examine or direct eyes toward

Example: Look at the question twice before blaming the options.

Meaning: to think about the past

Example: When she looked back, the struggle felt worth it.

Meaning: to consider inferior

Example: Never look down on someone doing honest work.

Meaning: to search

Example: He looked for his pen like a detective at a crime scene.

Meaning: to await with pleasure

Example: I look forward to seeing the final result.

Meaning: to investigate

Example: The committee looked into the complaint.

Meaning: to watch without joining

Example: People looked on while the magician fooled everyone.

Meaning: to be careful

Example: Look out, the step is broken.

Meaning: to inspect quickly

Example: Look over your answers before submitting.

Meaning: to search for information or improve

Example: Look up unfamiliar words instead of guessing proudly.

Meaning: to respect or admire

Example: Many students look up to a teacher who explains clearly.

Meaning: to move toward or contribute to

Example: Good sleep makes for better concentration.

Meaning: to understand or interpret

Example: What do you make of this strange clue?

Meaning: to escape quickly

Example: The thief made off with the bag.

Meaning: to understand or distinguish

Example: I could not make out the handwriting.

Meaning: to invent, form, or reconcile

Example: He made up an excuse so creative it deserved marks in fiction.

Meaning: to compensate for

Example: Hard work can make up for a slow start.

Meaning: to start living in a place

Example: They moved in before the paint had fully dried.

Meaning: to stop thinking about the past and continue

Example: After one bad test, move on and fix the pattern.

Meaning: to die

Example: The old poet passed away, but his lines remained alive.

Meaning: to faint or distribute

Example: He nearly passed out after seeing the electricity bill.

Meaning: to ignore or skip

Example: The committee passed over his application due to missing documents.

Meaning: to repay

Example: He paid back the loan after selling his old bike.

Meaning: to bring good results or repay fully

Example: Daily practice paid off in the final exam.

Meaning: to choose or identify

Example: She picked out the correct answer from four confusing options.

Meaning: to lift, collect, or learn

Example: He picked up English by reading cricket commentary.

Meaning: to indicate or mention

Example: The teacher pointed out the hidden error.

Meaning: to express clearly

Example: She put across her idea in one sharp sentence.

Meaning: to save or ignore temporarily

Example: Put aside ten minutes daily for revision.

Meaning: to store

Example: Put away your phone before it wins the study session.

Meaning: to write or insult

Example: Put down the main points before you forget them.

Meaning: to postpone

Example: Do not put off revision until panic becomes the teacher.

Meaning: to wear or increase

Example: Put on a sweater before the cold starts negotiating.

Meaning: to extinguish or publish

Example: The firefighters put out the blaze.

Meaning: to connect by phone or make someone experience

Example: The operator put me through to the office.

Meaning: to raise or tolerate

Example: They put up a notice outside the hall.

Meaning: to tolerate

Example: She put up with the noise because exams were near.

Meaning: to meet or find by chance

Example: I ran across a useful rule in an old guidebook.

Meaning: to chase

Example: The child ran after the ice-cream cart like destiny was leaving.

Meaning: to escape

Example: The dog ran away during the fireworks.

Meaning: to meet unexpectedly or collide with

Example: He ran into his teacher at the book fair.

Meaning: to become exhausted

Example: We ran out of time during the mock test.

Meaning: to hit with a vehicle or review quickly

Example: Go over the notes, do not run over them like a truck.

Meaning: to say goodbye to someone leaving

Example: The family saw him off at the station.

Meaning: to detect deception or continue to the end

Example: The examiner saw through the copied answer.

Meaning: to reserve or reject

Example: Set aside some money for books.

Meaning: to delay progress

Example: The injury set back his training by a month.

Meaning: to begin and seem likely to continue

Example: Winter set in earlier than expected.

Meaning: to start a journey or cause to start

Example: They set off before sunrise.

Meaning: to begin with a purpose or explain

Example: The report sets out the main reasons.

Meaning: to establish or arrange

Example: They set up a small library in the village.

Meaning: to display proudly

Example: He showed off his new phone until the battery died.

Meaning: to appear or arrive

Example: He showed up late with the confidence of a chief guest.

Meaning: to close or stop operating

Example: The factory shut down during the strike.

Meaning: to take a seat

Example: Sit down before the lecture becomes long.

Meaning: to solve or arrange

Example: Sort out your doubts before they become a crowd.

Meaning: to speak louder or express opinion

Example: Speak up if you know the answer.

Meaning: to support or be ready

Example: A real friend stands by you during failure.

Meaning: to represent or tolerate

Example: WHO stands for World Health Organization.

Meaning: to be noticeable

Example: Her neat handwriting stood out in the pile of answer sheets.

Meaning: to defend

Example: Stand up for what is right, even if the room is quiet.

Meaning: to resign

Example: The minister stepped down after the scandal.

Meaning: to continue with or follow

Example: Stick to your timetable even when laziness campaigns hard.

Meaning: to resemble an older family member

Example: She takes after her mother in both looks and stubbornness.

Meaning: to separate into pieces

Example: He took apart the radio and then looked for courage.

Meaning: to remove

Example: The teacher took away the cheat sheet with surgical calm.

Meaning: to withdraw a statement or return something

Example: He took back his words after seeing the proof.

Meaning: to write or remove

Example: Take down this formula before the board is erased.

Meaning: to understand or deceive

Example: The topic was hard to take in at first.

Meaning: to remove or leave the ground

Example: The plane took off while passengers finally stopped calling relatives.

Meaning: to accept responsibility or employ

Example: She took on extra work before the festival.

Meaning: to remove or extract

Example: Take out the unnecessary words from the sentence.

Meaning: to assume control

Example: The new manager took over the branch.

Meaning: to start a hobby or occupy space/time

Example: He took up cycling after promising to be healthy.

Meaning: to discuss

Example: Talk over the plan before spending money.

Meaning: to demolish

Example: The old wall was torn down for safety.

Meaning: to consider carefully

Example: Think over the offer before saying yes.

Meaning: to discard

Example: Do not throw away old notes before checking them.

Meaning: to reject or expel

Example: The proposal was thrown out by the committee.

Meaning: to refuse entry

Example: Late candidates were turned away at the gate.

Meaning: to reject or reduce volume

Example: She turned down the offer because the timing was bad.

Meaning: to submit or go to bed

Example: Turn in your assignment before the portal closes.

Meaning: to become

Example: The small argument turned into a full family debate.

Meaning: to switch off or disgust

Example: Turn off the fan when you leave.

Meaning: to switch on

Example: Turn on the light before reading the fine print.

Meaning: to happen in a particular way or attend

Example: The easy-looking question turned out to be a trap.

Meaning: to flip or transfer control

Example: Turn over the page only when told.

Meaning: to arrive or increase volume

Example: He turned up after everyone had finished waiting.

Meaning: to consume completely

Example: Do not use up all your energy on the first section.

Meaning: to stop sleeping

Example: Wake up before the alarm starts questioning your life choices.

Meaning: to leave suddenly in protest

Example: The workers walked out after the talks failed.

Meaning: to be careful

Example: Watch out for negative marking.

Meaning: to become exhausted or damaged

Example: The old shoes wore out after one rainy season.

Meaning: to solve or exercise

Example: She worked out the answer using a simple diagram.

Meaning: to note in writing

Example: Write down new words before they escape.

Meaning: to stop paying attention

Example: He zoned out during the lecture and returned during homework.

Meaning: to focus attention on

Example: The police zeroed in on the suspect after checking the footage.

Meaning: to reduce to the main point

Example: The whole argument boiled down to one missing signature.

Meaning: to face a difficulty

Example: The team came up against a strict deadline.

Meaning: to do again

Example: The teacher asked him to do over the messy assignment.

Meaning: to use as a source

Example: The writer drew on childhood memories for the story.

Meaning: to make progress

Example: She got ahead by revising while others only planned.

Meaning: to oppose or violate

Example: His statement went against the evidence.

Meaning: to prevent

Example: The heavy rain kept us from leaving.

Meaning: to stop doing something

Example: Leave off arguing and start solving the question.

Meaning: to meet expectations

Example: The film did not live up to the hype.

Meaning: to remember the past

Example: He looked back on his hostel days with a smile.

Meaning: to watch carefully for

Example: Look out for traps in article questions.

Meaning: to manage with what is available

Example: We made do with one torch during the power cut.

Meaning: to admit a mistake

Example: He owned up after the teacher found the missing chalk.

Meaning: to make something seem less important

Example: The minister played down the controversy.

Meaning: to succeed in doing something difficult

Example: She pulled off a high score despite starting late.

Meaning: to withdraw

Example: The sponsor pulled out at the last moment.

Meaning: to recover from difficulty or illness

Example: The patient pulled through after a tense night.

Meaning: to propose

Example: She put forward a practical solution.

Meaning: to eliminate or exclude

Example: The doctor ruled out a serious infection.

Meaning: to take care of

Example: Please see to the arrangements before guests arrive.

Meaning: to summon or call someone

Example: They sent for a doctor when the fever rose.

Meaning: to become calm or stable

Example: Settle down and read the question carefully.

Meaning: to express opinion openly

Example: She spoke out against unfair treatment.

Meaning: to persuade

Example: He talked me into joining the debate.

Meaning: to persuade someone not to do something

Example: She talked him out of buying a useless gadget.

Meaning: to distinguish

Example: The twins are hard to tell apart.

Meaning: to invent or create mentally

Example: He thought up a clever excuse, but the attendance register disagreed.

Meaning: to wear something to test fit

Example: Try on the jacket before buying it.

Meaning: to test

Example: Try out the new method on a small set first.

Meaning: to prepare for activity

Example: Warm up before running unless you want your legs to protest.

Meaning: to remove by water

Example: The rain washed away the chalk marks.

Meaning: to spend effort improving

Example: Work on weak topics before chasing new ones.

Meaning: to finish

Example: Wrap up the revision before dinner.
